phases.title: Prepare the invasion
phases.summary: Offshore bases put more fighters within reach of Sicily. Allied bombers attacked the fields the Axis needed to defend the island.

phases.title: Cover the landings
phases.summary: Fighters flew from offshore bases. Axis raids still reached the assault area, and Allied fire scattered a follow-up troop lift.

phases.title: Support the advance
phases.summary: Flying from Sicilian fields, fighters covered warships off Syracuse. Fighter-bombers struck roads and ports used by the Axis as the Allied armies advanced.

phases.title: Try to close the strait
phases.summary: Allied aircraft attacked the approaches and crossing points. The Axis kept enough of the ferry system working to evacuate much of its force.

sites.name: Gela assault sector
sites.precision: Representative point for western landing cover

formations.name: 33rd Fighter Group
formations.summary: Warhawks patrolled during the landings on Pantelleria, later operated from the island, and covered the Sicilian landings. The July reports place the group's move to Licata on different dates.

formations.name: 31st Fighter Group
formations.summary: Flew landing cover from Gozo and moved to Ponte Olivo and then Termini.

formations.name: No. 244 Wing
formations.summary: Flying units and ground parties reached Pachino in stages. The aircraft arrived on 13 July.

formations.name: Schnellkampfgeschwader 10
formations.summary: The 10 July ground-attack return lists elements of this wing at Gerbini, San Pietro and Montecorvino. Some Gruppen were split between island and mainland fields.

formations.name: 52nd Troop Carrier Wing
formations.summary: Aircraft carried the follow-up lift for the 504th Combat Team.

formations.name: 1st Parachute Brigade
formations.summary: Its objective was to seize Primosole Bridge and open a route towards Catania.

formations.name: 1st Airlanding Brigade
formations.summary: Its objective was to secure Ponte Grande on the approach to Syracuse.

formations.name: No. 92 Squadron RAF
formations.summary: Pilots patrolled the beaches en route from Malta to Pachino on 13 July. They covered ships off Syracuse on 16 July and escorted attacks on the Messina crossings on 16 August.

formations.name: No. 242 Squadron RAF
formations.summary: On 10 July its fighters engaged aircraft attacking the invasion force. The RAF narrative describes an interception while a Heinkel was firing on landing craft.

cases.title: Pantelleria becomes a forward base
cases.summary: After air and naval bombardment, Pantelleria surrendered on 11 June. Its airfield later supported fighters for the western landings.

evidence.title: Operation Corkscrew
evidence.note: The date refers to surrender. The RAF narrative places the 33rd Fighter Group on Pantelleria by early July.

evidence.locator: 33d Fighter Group, combat history and station list, June 1943
evidence.title: Patrols over the landing
evidence.note: The group history records fighter patrols as Allied troops came ashore. Its station list still places the group at Sousse in Tunisia on the surrender date.

formationRoles.fg33: Patrolled during the Allied landing after the surrender.

cases.title: The 33rd Fighter Group moves forward
cases.summary: About a week after the surrender, the group moved its base from Tunisia to Pantelleria. From there its Warhawks could cover the western Sicilian beaches in July. Two US histories differ by one day on the move.

formationRoles.fg33: Relocation from Sousse, dated 18 or 19 June.

evidence.title: Wing chronology · 18 June
evidence.note: The wing dates the move to Pantelleria to 18 June, following the 9 June move to Sousse.

evidence.title: USAF station list · 19 June
evidence.note: Maurer lists Pantelleria from 19 June. The different dates do not identify separate air and ground echelons.

cases.title: Spitfires stage through Gozo
cases.summary: A temporary airfield on Gozo added capacity for short-range fighters. The 31st Fighter Group flew Spitfires from there during the invasion.

evidence.locator: Preparation of Tactical Bases and D-Day fighter plan
evidence.title: Offshore basing
evidence.note: The date is the early-July checkpoint for Malta’s operational control of Spitfire units. The narrative places the group at Gozo by early July.

cases.title: The Gerbini complex comes under sustained attack
cases.summary: Heavy bombers struck Gerbini and its satellite fields. Allied assessments describe widespread disruption before the landings, with some aircraft still serviceable in the complex.

evidence.title: Bomb loads and field condition
evidence.note: The two bomb loads cover the same 3–9 July target complex under separate commands. Seven satellites and the main field were reported unserviceable around D-Day.

evidence.title: Location of the main field
evidence.note: The map anchor is Gerbini-Main. The directory lists additional satellite strips with different historical coverage from the pre-invasion Allied report.

cases.title: Ladbroke · gliders on the approach to Syracuse
cases.summary: A glider assault sought to hold Ponte Grande. Wind, navigation difficulties and premature releases scattered the force and brought gliders down at sea.

evidence.title: Ponte Grande objective
evidence.note: The map marks the bridge objective. The gliders came down at scattered locations on land and at sea.

cases.title: D-Day · fighters over the beaches
cases.summary: Spitfires and Warhawks covered the landings from Malta, Gozo and Pantelleria. German and Italian aircraft still reached ships and troops around the western assault beaches.

evidence.locator: Section XXXVI, Fighter Cover and Air Support
evidence.title: Western Naval Task Force report
evidence.note: Approximate cover rate across CENT, DIME and JOSS. Enemy tracks cover 02:45 on 10 July to 18:15 on 12 July and may include repeat flights.

evidence.title: Axis attacks reached the ships
evidence.note: The RAF narrative records the loss of USS Maddox to bombing in the DIME sector on 10 July.

evidence.locator: Chapter 14, pp. 450–452, fighter cover on 10 July
evidence.title: How much protection reached the fleet?
evidence.note: The long flight from offshore fields limited time over the beaches. The US Navy reported gaps in cover over the American sectors. Allied air commanders pointed to the scale of their patrols and lower ship losses than the Navy had feared. The number of ships saved by patrols remains unknown.

evidence.locator: Chapter 3, printed p. 52, fighting on 10 July
evidence.title: Patrols intercepted attacks on shipping
evidence.note: At 04:50 No. 242 Squadron engaged a Heinkel firing on landing craft. Later, ten Warhawks of the 33rd Fighter Group attacked German fighters they saw dropping bombs on shipping east of Licata. The US pilots claimed two destroyed and two damaged. The account gives no independent German loss match or count of ships saved.

formationRoles.fg33: Warhawks intercepted aircraft bombing ships east of Licata on 10 July.
formationRoles.sq242: Spitfires intercepted an aircraft attacking landing craft on 10 July. The account gives no precise position.

cases.title: Pachino · captured on invasion day
cases.summary: British forces took the landing ground by noon. The field had been ploughed up. Engineers and servicing parties had work ahead before squadrons could use it.

evidence.locator: The First Fighter Wing in Sicily and Comparison with the Air Plan
evidence.title: Capture and engineering
evidence.note: Advance officers inspected the strip on invasion day. On 12 July visiting Spitfires refuelled on their way back to Malta. The wing’s air echelon followed on 13 July.

evidence.title: Engineering return
evidence.note: Work began on 10 July. The engineering staff entered 14 July in its operational column.

formationRoles.wing244: The wing leader and advance officers inspected the ploughed strip. Its flying echelon arrived on 13 July.

cases.title: German ground-attack aircraft on 10 July
cases.summary: The German return splits SKG 10's ground-attack aircraft between Sicily and the mainland. The separate fighter returns identify German and Italian units at Sicilian fields.

evidence.locator: Appendix 3, printed appendix p. 9, Ground Attack, 10 July
evidence.title: II./SKG 10 · Gerbini and Montecorvino
evidence.note: The zero for serviceable aircraft at Gerbini is explicit. The mainland detachment has a separate line in the same return compiled from German records.

evidence.locator: Appendix 3, printed appendix p. 9, Ground Attack, 10 July
evidence.title: III./SKG 10 · San Pietro and Montecorvino
evidence.note: San Pietro is the Biscari airfield. These are aircraft held and serviceable at each station.

evidence.locator: Appendix 3, printed appendix p. 9, Ground Attack, 10 July
evidence.title: IV./SKG 10 · Gerbini
evidence.note: Aircraft serviceability and runway condition are separate observations.

formationRoles.skg10: Three component Gruppen appear in this ground-attack return.

cases.title: Gela · friendly fire on the follow-up lift
cases.summary: Transports carrying the 504th Combat Team approached after Axis attacks on the invasion fleet. Ship and shore batteries opened fire. The formations broke up and many drops missed the intended area.

evidence.title: Outcomes for the transports
evidence.note: The denominator is aircraft departing Tunisia. The Army history reports aircraft that failed to return and badly damaged aircraft. The total does not assign each loss to a specific battery.

cases.title: Comiso · aircraft found on a captured field
cases.summary: The RAF narrative records occupation on the night of 11 July and lists the field as serviceable by 13 July. Inspections counted aircraft left at the field.

evidence.locator: Air offensive results table and Comparison with the Air Plan
evidence.title: Post-capture inspection
evidence.note: The inspection count does not establish when each aircraft was abandoned or damaged.

cases.title: Ponte Olivo · preparing and occupying the field
cases.summary: The U.S. 1st Infantry Division took the field on 12 July. The RAF narrative places the 31st Fighter Group’s arrival on 13 July. The tactical air force records the field as operational on 15 July and lists the group there on 16 July.

evidence.locator: The Landing of XII Air Support Command
evidence.title: Gozo to Ponte Olivo
evidence.note: The group’s Spitfires had supplied landing cover from Gozo. Arrival and capture are separately dated.

evidence.title: Engineering return
evidence.note: The engineering staff dates the start of work to 12 July and the field’s operational status to 15 July.

evidence.locator: Appendix I, printed p. 158, 31st Fighter Group
evidence.title: The group in the build-up return
evidence.note: The return lists the 307th, 308th and 309th Squadrons together at Ponte Olivo on 16 July. It does not date each aircraft’s arrival or first sortie.

cases.title: Biscari · two accounts of the capture date
cases.summary: The RAF summary dates occupation to 12 July and excludes Biscari from fields serviceable by 13 July. The U.S. Military Academy study dates the 45th Division taking the airfield to 14 July.

evidence.title: RAF account · 12 July
evidence.note: The RAF account does not give a serviceable date for this airfield.

evidence.title: U.S. account · 14 July
evidence.note: The sources give different dates and do not establish if their thresholds for occupation match.

cases.title: Pachino · the first fighter wing arrives
cases.summary: No. 244 Wing’s fighters landed after their first patrols. Mobile plotting, signals, fuel and ammunition enabled operations. Squadron parties handled much of the Spitfire IX servicing.

evidence.locator: The First Fighter Wing in Sicily, 13 July, citing the wing ORB
evidence.title: Operational handover
evidence.note: Ground personnel came in stages. The date marks the air echelon’s arrival and local readiness.

evidence.title: A patrol ended at the new field
evidence.note: Eleven pilots left Luqa on Malta, patrolled the beaches and landed at Pachino. Other pilots flew directly to the field. The daily total covers the transition between bases.

evidence.locator: Appendix B, printed p. 25, departures for Pachino
evidence.title: The wing moved in stages
evidence.note: RAF Malta dates the departures of Nos. 1 SAAF, 92, 145 and 601 Squadrons to 13 July. No. 417 Squadron RCAF followed on 16 July.

cases.title: Fustian · under fire en route to Primosole
cases.summary: The British 1st Parachute Brigade went in to seize the bridge. Friendly anti-aircraft fire, scattering and German resistance complicated the assault. Ground forces later secured the crossing.

evidence.title: Bridge objective and friendly fire
evidence.note: The bridge anchor locates the objective. Fire and landings were spread across the approach and drop areas.

cases.title: Pachino · patrols before the ground party arrived
cases.summary: By the time No. 92 Squadron’s ground personnel reached Pachino, its pilots had already flown two patrols. A damaged Spitfire returned to base on the second. Three more patrols followed that day.

evidence.title: Flying from the new base
evidence.note: The diary counts patrols, each of which could involve several aircraft. It establishes flying activity by this date. The time of the first take-off from the strip remains open.

evidence.title: Engineering return
evidence.note: The field is listed as operational on 14 July. The wing and squadron accounts document landings there the preceding day.

cases.title: Licata · Warhawks come ashore
cases.summary: The tactical air force listed the 33rd Fighter Group at Licata on 16 July. US station histories date its move from Pantelleria to about 18 July. The RAF recorded little damage from raids on Licata and Ponte Olivo on the night of the 16th.

evidence.locator: The Landing of XII Air Support Command, 16 July
evidence.title: Pantelleria to Licata
evidence.note: The RAF places the arrival at Licata on 16 July. The port and beachhead had fallen on invasion day.

evidence.locator: Appendix I, printed p. 158, 16 July build-up
evidence.title: Three squadrons listed at Licata
evidence.note: The tactical air force lists the group's 58th, 59th and 60th Squadrons at Licata on 16 July.

evidence.title: Group station entry · about 18 July
evidence.note: The US station list dates Licata to approximately 18 July. The sources do not resolve which echelon accounts for the two-day difference.

cases.title: Axis air forces withdraw from Sicily
cases.summary: The RAF narrative reports a sharp reduction in aircraft remaining on the island as Axis units withdrew. Aircraft moved to another base, left behind and lost in combat had different outcomes.

evidence.locator: The Defeat of the Axis Air Forces
evidence.title: German aircraft remaining on Sicily
evidence.note: Separate island-wide inventories.

evidence.locator: The Defeat of the Axis Air Forces, Italian documents
evidence.title: Italian fighters on Sicily, 22 July
evidence.note: The four serviceable aircraft are included in the 28 on hand.

cases.title: Pachino · cover for ships off Syracuse
cases.summary: Eight aircraft covered shipping off Syracuse. The squadron diary identifies Nelson and Rodney and describes a bombardment that evening. Nelson’s service chronology places her bombardment later. Pachino was the squadron’s operating station.

evidence.title: A dated task for the island-based squadron
evidence.note: The entry names both ships and orders a move to Cassibile at dawn. The next diary entry is headed Cassibile.

evidence.title: A different sequence in the ship’s chronology
evidence.note: Rodney rejoined Force H on 16 July. The ship history places Nelson’s Catania bombardment after the torpedoing of Indomitable early on 17 July. The squadron’s shipping patrol is documented independently of that timing.

cases.title: Biscari · the strip enters the engineering return
cases.summary: After the two accounts of capture, the engineering return records another sequence. Work began on 16 July and the field was listed as operational on 19 July. The first unit sortie from Biscari remains undated here.

evidence.title: Engineering return
evidence.note: Biscari was an existing airfield requiring repair or improvement. The operational column describes the field. It supplies neither a flying unit nor a time of take-off.

cases.title: Palermo falls · the advance turns east
cases.summary: The Seventh Army took Palermo and turned east. During the western advance, aircraft struck communications and targets of opportunity.

evidence.title: Western advance
evidence.note: The pin locates the port. The described air activity covers the wider advance.

cases.title: The 31st Fighter Group moves to Termini
cases.summary: The group shifted from Ponte Olivo to the north coast. XII Air Support Command retained operational control.

evidence.locator: XII Air Support Command following 24 July
evidence.title: Forward station on the north coast
evidence.note: The group moved on 27 July. The advanced headquarters moved on 28 July.

cases.title: Catania falls · the front moves north
cases.summary: British forces entered Catania after the German withdrawal. The air campaign had attacked Catania and the roads and rail links supporting the Axis around Etna.

evidence.title: Isolation of the battlefield
evidence.note: The date is for entry into the city. The July suppression of airfields around Catania and Gerbini is a separate event.

cases.title: Messina · the strait remains open
cases.summary: Bombing interrupted some crossings. On 16 August No. 92 Squadron covered Warhawks attacking shipping, escorted Baltimores to Messina and patrolled over Allied warships. Axis troops continued to cross to Italy.

evidence.locator: Form 540, 16 August 1943, 07:25 patrol and later missions
evidence.title: No. 92 Squadron covered the attacks
evidence.note: Eight pilots escorted the Warhawks, and six escorted the Baltimores later that morning. An afternoon patrol covered warships southeast of Taormina. The diary records these missions. The fate of individual ferries requires separate craft records.

evidence.title: Allied attacks on the crossings
evidence.note: The daylight figure covers 8–17 August and includes attacks along the mainland approaches. The Wellington average refers to the nights of 8/9 to 13/14 August against evacuation beaches.

evidence.locator: Chapter XXI, The End of the Campaign, note 9
evidence.title: Allied claims and Axis craft records
evidence.note: The Army history juxtaposes Allied air claims and the Axis craft register. The ship losses have different cause and reporting coverage. This is no basis for a matched success rate.

evidence.locator: Chapter XXI, The End of the Campaign, note 21, German report of 17 August
evidence.title: German evacuation return
evidence.note: Wounded are included in the personnel total. The Italian evacuation falls outside these figures.

evidence.title: Ferry network and air defence
evidence.note: The evacuation used separate crossing routes and concentrated anti-aircraft defences. The campaign range on the map starts with the German main evacuation, which was underway by 11 August.

formationRoles.sq92: On 16 August the squadron escorted attacks on shipping and flew a warship patrol.
